title: Tara Fixes the Wobbly Birdhouse
markdown:
Tara wore overalls patterned like a treasure map. She wanted to fix a birdhouse, but oh, it wobbled like jelly. She opened her toolbox. Inside: shiny metal screws, bendy plastic hinges, and smooth wooden pegs.

“Which is best?” she wondered.

Nibble the mouse peeked out. “Squeak?”

Tara pointed at the wobbly birdhouse. “I need to make it strong.”

She picked it up. Soft wood. The perch was loose. She held a wooden peg. Smooth. Then a metal screw. Cool and hard.

“This metal,” Tara whispered, “feels like it could hold up a tower.”

She bent a plastic hinge. It sprang back. “And this plastic is perfect for things that move. Like a door.”

Auntie June came in, smelling of cinnamon. “A puzzle?”

Tara showed her the toolbox. “I know now, Auntie June. Wood is for building. Metal is super strong. Plastic is bendy for doors.”

She used the shiny metal screws. Screeeech went the screwdriver. The birdhouse walls grew firm. Then she attached the bendy plastic hinges for the door. Click, click. It swung with a bounce. Lastly she put in the smooth wooden peg for the perch. Tap, tap. It stood.

The birdhouse did not wobble. A robin landed and chirped.

“You did it!” Auntie June hugged Tara tight. Nibble squeaked.

“Wood is lovely for building, metal is strong, and plastic is flexible for moving parts,” Auntie June smiled.

Tara beamed. The walls held because of the screws. The door moved because of the hinges. The perch stayed because of the peg. She looked around the workshop — wood, metal, plastic — and chose, next time, with her fingers first.
